newsitem.title: UK: ICCO sees 1996/97 world cocoa crop at 2.485 mln T.
newsitem.headline: ICCO sees 1996/97 world cocoa crop at 2.485 mln T.

text.p: The International Cocoa Organisation (ICCO) Council on Wednesday forecast world cocoa production at 2.485 million tonnes in 1996/97 against 2.803 million tonnes in 1995/96.

The Council, which comprises top cocoa producing and consuming nations, forecast world cocoa grindings (consumption) at 2.710 million tonnes in 1996/97 compared with the year-ago level of 2.684 million.
An official from the ICCO said the Council endorsed the estimates drawn up by the ICCO Secretariat despite earlier reservations from four producing nation delegates.
Delegates from the Ivory Coast, Ghana, Brazil and Malaysia said the ICCO's estimates were not in line with their own national estimates.
"The figures stand as they are," an ICCO spokeswoman told reporters after the Council meeting broke up on Wednesday.
ICCO estimates are used to help determine annual production targets under the grouping's voluntary scheme to help balance world supply and demand.
